assumptions.statement: Harness, provider/auth route, model, tool policy, cache policy, workload, and billing policy are separate factors.
assumptions.validation: Controlled comparisons hold all but one factor fixed.

assumptions.statement: Tool definitions, system instructions, skills, custom agents, and MCP registries consume input or cache-write tokens on a cold request.
assumptions.validation: Local Copilot CLI and Pi calibration records prompt-token usage under full, minimal, and zero-tool policies.

assumptions.statement: A stable reusable prefix can turn repeated input into cheaper cache reads, while prefix churn, model switches, idle expiry, and some compactions require new writes.
assumptions.validation: Hot continuation pilots and explicit low/high stability challenge points.

assumptions.statement: Quality depends on task difficulty, model tier, relevant-tool success, tool confusion, provider failures, retries, verification strength, and compaction loss.
assumptions.validation: Wide one-at-a-time and joint challenge points; no empirical-real-world claim is identified.

assumptions.statement: Wall time is mediated by model calls, processed context, tool latency, retries, approvals, parallelizable work, coordination overhead, and conflicts.
assumptions.validation: Concurrency, latency, failure, and conflict challenges.

assumptions.statement: Token rates and Copilot plan allowances equal the official public values captured on 2026-09-04.
assumptions.validation: Refresh the rate-card source before later decisions because prices are time-varying.

assumptions.statement: Provider token value, marginal cash outlay, allocated subscription fee, and economic loss are different estimands.
assumptions.validation: The model emits all four ledgers and never substitutes Pi's catalog estimate for Copilot cash billing.

assumptions.statement: A monthly subscription may have zero marginal cash cost while credits remain, but the fee still has an allocated cost and an opportunity cost.
assumptions.validation: Low-, medium-, and high-volume portfolios plus allowance-exhaustion challenges.

assumptions.statement: Matched scenarios share latent task difficulty, tool reliability, provider reliability, and human-review draws through named SHA-256 substreams.
assumptions.validation: Same-behavior-label negative-control tests and paired hypothesis analysis.

assumptions.statement: No simulation-only contrast identifies which harness is better on real repositories.
assumptions.validation: The real-world supremacy hypotheses are explicitly not-identifiable; matched tasks with a fixed external verifier are required.

assumptions.statement: Removing irrelevant tools reduces context and selection confusion, but removing required tools lowers success and can increase retries or human rework.
assumptions.validation: Both tool-sprawl and under-provisioned challenge points are included.

assumptions.statement: Cheap planning and routine execution with stronger verification can improve cost efficiency when routing errors remain bounded.
assumptions.validation: Compare fixed-tier policies against phase routing under easy, hard, and verification-heavy workloads.
